So, $x = 2$.

(C) Nuclear forces are spin dependent.

(D) Nuclear forces are central and charge independent.

(C) Nuclear forces are spin dependent but charge independent.

(D) Nuclear force is attractive in nature. It is a non central force, meaning it does not depend upon the distance between the particles but rather upon their orientation. Nuclear force is stronger if the spin is parallel; and weak if it is anti parallel.

(E) The negative value (less quantity) of packing fraction indicates that the isotope is stable. Positive value of packing fraction implies unstable (radioactive) nucleus. Also, the stability of the nucleus is inversely proportional to the value of the packing fraction.

The binding energy per nucleon of $^{209}_{83}Bi$ is _______ MeV.
$[\text{Take } m(^{209}_{83}Bi) = 208.980388 \, u, \, m_p = 1.007825 \, u, \, m_n = 1.008665 \, u, \, 1 \, u = 931 \, \text{MeV}/c^2]$
questions.solution:
For the nucleus $^{209}_{83}Bi$, the number of protons is $Z = 83$ and the number of neutrons is $N = 209 - 83 = 126$.

Mass of $83$ protons $= 83 \times 1.007825 = 83.649475 \, u$

Mass of $126$ neutrons $= 126 \times 1.008665 = 127.091790 \, u$

Total mass of the nucleons $= 83.649475 + 127.091790 = 210.741265 \, u$

The mass defect $\Delta m$ is given by:

$\Delta m = \text{Total mass of nucleons} - \text{Mass of nucleus}$

$\Delta m = 210.741265 - 208.980388 = 1.760877 \, u$

The total binding energy ($BE$) is:

$BE = \Delta m \times 931 \, \text{MeV}$

$BE = 1.760877 \times 931 = 1639.376 \, \text{MeV}$

The binding energy per nucleon is:

$\dfrac{BE}{A} = \dfrac{1639.376}{209} \approx 7.84 \, \text{MeV}$

Answer: $7.84$

questions.question: A nucleus of mass $M$ emits $\gamma$-ray photon of frequency $v$. The loss of internal energy by the nucleus is: [Take $c$ as the speed of electromagnetic wave]

Energy of $\gamma$ ray $\left[{E}_{γ}\right] = hv$

Momentum of $\gamma$ ray $\left[{P}_{γ}\right] = \dfrac{h}{λ} = \dfrac{hv}{c}$
Total momentum is conserved.

$\overset{→}{P}\gamma + \overset{→}{P}Nu = 0$
where $\overset{→}{P}Nu =$ momentum of decayed nuclei

$⇒ {P}_{γ} = {P}_{Nu}$
$⇒ \dfrac{hv}{c} = {P}_{Nu}$
$⇒ KE$ of nuclei

$= \dfrac{1}{2}M{v}^{2} = \dfrac{\left({P}_{Nu}\right)2}{2M} = \dfrac{1}{2M}\left[\dfrac{hv}{c}\right]2$
Loss in internal energy $= {E}_{γ} + {KE}_{Nu}$
$= hv + \dfrac{1}{2M}\left[\dfrac{hv}{c}\right]2$
$= hv\left[1 + \dfrac{hv}{2M{c}^{2}}\right]$

questions.question: Two nuclei of mass number $3$ combine with another nucleus of mass number $4$ to yield a nucleus of mass number $10$. If the binding energy per nucleon for the mass numbers $3$, $4$ and $10$ are $5.6$ MeV, $7.4$ MeV and $6.1$ MeV, respectively, then in the process, $\Delta Mc^2 = $ _____ MeV.
questions.solution:
The nuclear reaction is given by:

$2 X^{3} + Y^{4} \rightarrow Z^{10}$

The total binding energy of the reactants is the sum of the binding energies of the two nuclei of mass number $3$ and the nucleus of mass number $4$.

Binding energy of reactants $= 2 \times (3 \times 5.6) + (4 \times 7.4)$

$= 33.6 + 29.6 = 63.2$ MeV

The total binding energy of the product nucleus of mass number $10$ is:

Binding energy of product $= 10 \times 6.1 = 61.0$ MeV

The change in mass energy $\Delta M c^2$ is equal to the difference in the total binding energies of the reactants and the product.

$\Delta M c^2 = |63.2 - 61.0| = 2.2$ MeV

Answer: $2.2$

questions.solution:
The nuclear reaction for the proton bombardment of Lithium is:

$^{7}_{3}\text{Li} + ^{1}_{1}\text{H} \rightarrow 2 ^{4}_{2}\text{He}$

The mass defect ($\Delta m$) for the reaction is:

$\Delta m = m(^{7}_{3}\text{Li}) + m(^{1}_{1}\text{H}) - 2m(^{4}_{2}\text{He})$

$\Delta m = 7.0183 + 1.008 - 2(4.004)$

$\Delta m = 8.0263 - 8.008 = 0.0183 \text{ u}$

Energy released per reaction ($Q$) is:

$Q = \Delta m \times 931 \text{ MeV} = 0.0183 \times 931 \text{ MeV} = 17.0373 \text{ MeV}$

Number of moles of $^{7}_{3}\text{Li}$ in $\dfrac{7}{17.13} \text{ kg}$:

$n = \dfrac{\dfrac{7}{17.13} \times 10^3 \text{ g}}{7 \text{ g/mol}} = \dfrac{1000}{17.13} \text{ mol}$

Number of atoms of $^{7}_{3}\text{Li}$:

$N = n \times N_A = \dfrac{1000}{17.13} \times 6.0 \times 10^{23} = \dfrac{6}{17.13} \times 10^{26}$

Total energy released ($E$) is:

$E = N \times Q = \left(\dfrac{6}{17.13} \times 10^{26}\right) \times (17.0373 \times 10^6 \text{ eV})$

$E = \dfrac{102.2238}{17.13} \times 10^{32} \text{ eV} \approx 5.967 \times 10^{32} \text{ eV}$

Rounding to the nearest integer, we get $\alpha = 6$.

Answer: $6$

questions.question: Two radioactive substances A and B of mass numbers $200$ and $212$ respectively, shows spontaneous $\alpha$-decay with same $Q$ value of $1$ MeV. The ratio of energies of $\alpha$-rays produced by A and B is ________.
questions.solution:
In an $\alpha$-decay, the kinetic energy of the emitted $\alpha$-particle is given by the conservation of momentum and energy as:

$K_{\alpha} = \dfrac{A - 4}{A} Q$

where $A$ is the mass number of the parent nucleus.

For substance A ($A = 200$):

$K_{\alpha, A} = \dfrac{200 - 4}{200} Q = \dfrac{196}{200} Q$

For substance B ($A = 212$):

$K_{\alpha, B} = \dfrac{212 - 4}{212} Q = \dfrac{208}{212} Q$

The ratio of the energies of the $\alpha$-rays produced by A and B is:

$\dfrac{K_{\alpha, A}}{K_{\alpha, B}} = \dfrac{\dfrac{196}{200} Q}{\dfrac{208}{212} Q} = \dfrac{196}{200} \times \dfrac{212}{208}$

Simplifying the fractions:

$\dfrac{K_{\alpha, A}}{K_{\alpha, B}} = \dfrac{49}{50} \times \dfrac{53}{52} = \dfrac{2597}{2600}$

Answer: $\dfrac{2597}{2600}$
